method: Serial HTTPS GETs of approved source HTML only; normal TLS validation; no third-party photos saved. With --reuse-current, prior checks retain their original timestamps.
limitations: HTTP reachability is not photographic re-inspection, proof of every fine anatomical detail, interactive app navigation, or native-device verification.
buildAuthorization: PROHIBITED. Even complete coverage requires owner review and explicit separate later authorization before any build, release, scheduling, submission, or publishing.

illustrations.title: Cranial sutures: superior and posterior views
Typical vertebra: superior view with lateral inset
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A dry human thoracic vertebra in superior view shows the common vertebral plan. The assigned thoracic lateral inset, disc, and separate detail are not shown.

illustrations.title: Atlas (C1) from above and axis (C2) from the side
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: The human dry atlas and axis pair is photographed from above, but the assigned C2 lateral view is absent.

illustrations.title: Thoracic cage, anterior view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Targeted searches found no visually inspected dry human rib-cage photo with the sternum and cartilage arrangement. A Calisphere anterior human thorax dissection page surfaced and its caption was fetched, but the photograph itself was not visually inspected and the complete bone/cartilage plate cannot be confirmed; this is unavailable evidence, not proof that no suitable photo exists.

illustrations.title: Rib detail: head, tubercle and costal groove
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Two targeted searches yielded no visually inspected, provenance-checked human rib specimen photo showing the head, tubercle and costal groove; candidate illustrations/renders were excluded.

illustrations.title: Pectoral girdle relationships, anterior view (right side detailed)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Scapular surface photographs and a right anterior human glenohumeral dissection establish portions of the girdle. Clavicle, complete clavicle-scapula-humerus relationships, and ligament set are not covered.

illustrations.title: Right forearm, anterior view, with proximal-ulna inset
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A real human articulated radius-ulna specimen is shown anteriorly at the elbow. It is not the complete right forearm, interosseous membrane, or proximal-ulna lateral inset.

illustrations.title: Right hand, palmar view: carpals, metacarpals, phalanges
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: An assembled human hand skeleton photo covers carpals, metacarpals and phalanges. The source does not identify palmar/dorsal orientation or side, so it is not claimed as an exact right-palmar match.

illustrations.title: Right hip bone: lateral (left) and medial (right) views
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A dry human os coxae lateral view shows acetabulum and obturator foramen; a hip-joint dissection supplies limited context. Medial surface and laterality are unverified.

illustrations.title: Right leg, anterior view, with tibial-plateau inset
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A dry human tibia/fibula anterior pair corresponds to the main leg bones. The superior plateau inset, ankle mortise detail, and laterality are not documented.

illustrations.title: Right foot, dorsal view: tarsals, metatarsals, phalanges
Generic synovial joint in section
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A photographed human left elbow dissection is a specific synovial-joint example, not a generic section proving the full capsule, synovial lining/fluid, and external ligament layers.

illustrations.title: Right shoulder joint relationships, anterior view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A right anterior glenohumeral dissection opens the capsule and exposes the glenoid fossa. It does not cover the complete shoulder bones and ligament relationships in the diagram.

illustrations.title: Right knee: anterior layer (left) and deep cruciates, patella omitted (right)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Verified left medial knee and posterior popliteal-fossa dissections show joint structures and PCL. The anterior right-knee panel and full cruciate/collateral set remain incomplete; a newly surfaced right anterior Calisphere candidate was not visually inspected.

illustrations.title: Major body cavities with serous-space inset
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: No single verified human photograph covers the cavities, diaphragm, retroperitoneal kidney, and pleural-space inset. Sectional candidates did not meet this composite coverage.

illustrations.title: Four abdominal quadrants
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Quadrant boundaries are an abstract surface-location convention, not literal anatomy that a specimen photo can reproduce; no specifically identified real human example was verified.

illustrations.title: Nine abdominal regions
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Nine-region boundaries are an abstract surface mapping convention; no literal specimen counterpart was verified.

illustrations.title: Whole-body organ locations
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: No one verified human in-situ photograph shows the full set of labeled organs and retroperitoneal kidneys. A valid composite needs separately verified subject-specific sources.

illustrations.title: Anterior skeleton
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Verified human dry-bone photos give selected anterior skull, scapula, femur, tibia/fibula, hand, and foot examples. They do not form a complete articulated skeleton or include the full rib cage and other bones.

illustrations.title: Posterior skeleton
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Verified dry human photos show a posterior scapula and anterior/posterior femur pair. Most posterior axial and appendicular regions are absent.

illustrations.title: Axial and appendicular skeleton
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: The selected real specimens include skull and thoracic vertebra examples for axial bones, plus scapula, femur, tibia/fibula, hand and foot examples for appendicular bones. The hand and foot source pages were individually visually confirmed in their bone-specific records; this collection still does not form a complete skeleton or demonstrate the full division.

illustrations.title: Anterior skull: facial bones and openings
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A genuine anterior human skull specimen is verified. It is worn and unlabelled, so minor facial foramina and some boundaries are not clearly represented.

illustrations.title: Left lateral skull
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: No exact human dry-bone lateral skull photograph with credible specimen provenance and visual inspection was verified. The newly fetched similarly titled Commons candidate credits a medical illustrator and cannot be relied upon as a genuine dry bone specimen.

illustrations.title: Lateral vertebral column plate
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: No photographed dry human vertebral column with credible specimen provenance was verified; previously inspected display-column imagery did not establish a human dry-bone specimen.

illustrations.title: Regional vertebrae compared: cervical, thoracic, lumbar (superior view)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Human dry cervical and thoracic vertebra examples are verified in superior-compatible views. No comparable lumbar specimen or complete three-region comparison is present.

illustrations.title: Original body cavities
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: No verified human section photograph meets the composite body-cavity/diaphragm coverage; a page describing the NLM dataset is not an inspected specimen image.

illustrations.title: Elbow joint
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: A verified human elbow joint dissection is a relevant real example, but it does not reproduce all the original illustration labels and cross-sectional layers.

illustrations.title: Axial skeleton, anterior view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Verified photos cover anterior skull, cranial floor and a thoracic vertebra. A complete axial skeleton, ribs and full vertebral column are not covered.

illustrations.title: Appendicular skeleton, anterior view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Verified human specimens cover selected scapula, femur, tibia/fibula, hand and foot bones. They do not form the full appendicular skeleton and hand/foot laterality/view limits remain.

illustrations.title: Deep back muscles (trapezius and latissimus dorsi removed)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: human posterior deep-back and right scapular dissection photographs verify multifidus/rotator and scapular-region examples, but they do not jointly show the assigned unilateral lumbar quadratus lumborum plus intact-versus-removed erector spinae comparison.

illustrations.title: Deep thigh: anterior and posterior cutaways
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: the verified human right anterior thigh photo supports the vastus-intermedius region, but the source does not establish the full articularis-genus detail or the posterior semimembranosus cutaway.

illustrations.title: Calf: surface and cutaway
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: the inspected human specimen photograph directly shows the gastrocnemius–soleus junction, but it is an isolated medial specimen and does not include in-situ popliteus or tibialis posterior.

illustrations.title: Foot: plantar first layer and dorsal inset
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: two inspected Stanford photos confirm left plantar human specimens and deep plantar structures, but neither shows the assigned first plantar layer (abductor hallucis/flexor digitorum brevis) and the separate dorsal extensor-digitorum-brevis inset is not covered.

illustrations.title: Pelvic floor: levator ani, superior view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: a verified human male perineum/pelvic-diaphragm photograph names levator ani, but its perineal/superior fascia view does not match the assigned superior pelvic-floor view or establish the pubococcygeus and iliococcygeus bands.

illustrations.title: Face and neck muscles, right lateral view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: distinct inspected human face and left lateral-neck dissection photos offer regional examples, but named facial-muscle coverage is incomplete and the neck side/view does not match the right lateral composite.

illustrations.title: Anterior chest and shoulder muscles
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: human anterior thorax and right axilla source photos verify pectoral/intercostal examples, but not the full asymmetric superficial-to-deep chest, shoulder and abdominal muscle plate.

illustrations.title: Anterior arm: superficial and deep layers
Superficial back and scapular muscles
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: the inspected LibreTexts/BlueLink page includes one actual superficial posterior cadaver-back photo, but its letter markers are not independently decoded and not all assigned scapular structures are confirmed.

illustrations.title: Posterior lower limb: contextual overview
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: an inspected left posterolateral thigh photograph verifies gluteal and hamstring-region examples, but no retained source establishes the bilateral posterior overview through the calf and all depicted structures.

illustrations.title: Superficial muscles, anterior and posterior views
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: specific right shoulder/back, left posterior-lateral thigh/gluteal and anterior thorax source photographs provide regional examples, but no source set forms the whole-body paired superficial views or establishes all pinned muscles.

illustrations.title: Diaphragm: domes and inferior view
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Stanford's inspected human superior and inferior diaphragm photos verify those real views, but the assigned anterior coronal cutaway and comparative dome-height panel are missing.

illustrations.title: Rotator cuff: anterior and posterior views
Optic disc, macula and optic nerve head
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the fundus panel with a human fundus photograph and human optic-nerve-head histology. A fundus image does not show the nerve-head cutaway; macular/foveal detail and permission-qualified figure panels remain limitations.

illustrations.title: Brain, lateral surface: lobes and insula
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the lateral-lobe/insula diagram with one human lateral-dissection candidate and a verified medial-section photo. Candidate caption shows resected lateral cortex, but image inspection and exposed insula are not established.

illustrations.title: Brain, midsagittal view: callosum, diencephalon, ventricles
Eye in section: tunics, lens and vitreous chamber
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared full-eye section diagram against the available human fundus example only; it does not show cornea, tunics, lens or vitreous section. Full globe photo not verified.

illustrations.title: Ear in section: outer, middle and inner
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared ear-section diagram against the NLM historical human-ear photographic-work catalog. Catalog-level record lacks a reviewed individual plate; outer/middle/inner coverage remains unverified.

illustrations.title: Deep brain nuclei, coronal slice
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the coronal nuclei diagram with a human pathological coronal gross section. Source caption is edema, not basal nuclei; caudate, putamen and pallidum are not identified.

illustrations.title: Brainstem, cerebellum and spinal cord, midsagittal
Ventricles, CSF and meninges
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared CSF/ventricular and cranial meningeal panels with a cervical spinal meninges/roots dissection. It does not depict ventricular flow or cranial choroid plexus.

illustrations.title: Spinal cord in cross-section: gray matter, tracts and roots
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the cord diagram with transverse cord histology and a separate cervical root dissection. Histology does not identify colored tracts or roots; root photo is a different specimen/view.

illustrations.title: Spinal nerve: roots, ganglion and rami
The four major plexuses and the phrenic nerve
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: the already inspected Michigan human brachial-plexus dissections replace reliance on an organism-unconfirmed candidate for that region. The whole-body diagram still lacks verified cervical/lumbar/sacral plexus, phrenic-nerve and spinal-cord coverage as a combined set. No complete-plate link is approved.

illustrations.title: Median, ulnar and radial nerves of the right upper limb
Femoral and sciatic nerves of the right lower limb
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the femoral/sciatic diagram with a human sciatic-nerve file record. Sciatic photo itself was unavailable for visual inspection and no femoral nerve counterpart was confirmed.

illustrations.title: Cranial nerves I-VI, inferior surface of the brain
Cranial nerves VII-XII, brainstem and cerebellopontine angle
Anterior eye: chambers, aqueous humor and zonules
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: No source-page image was verified for a human anterior-segment specimen. A targeted NCBI eye-anatomy page fetch failed; no substitute drawing or model was accepted.

illustrations.title: Retina: cell chain (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the retinal cell-chain schematic with a human photoreceptor-cell record. Image not visually inspected and one cell cannot represent layered retinal organization or ganglion/bipolar cells.

illustrations.title: Inner ear: vestibule, canals and cochlea
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared labyrinth schematic with human organ-of-Corti microscopy. Candidate image was not visually inspected and does not show vestibule, utricle, saccule or semicircular canals.

illustrations.title: Cochlear ducts and the organ of Corti (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared the duct/cell schematic with two human cochlear microscopy articles; the SEM organ-of-Corti surface was visually inspected. It does not show the whole duct compartments or complete schematic cross-section.

illustrations.title: Smell and taste: pathways and receptor cells (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: Compared smell/taste panels with human olfactory mucosa micrograph metadata and OpenStax taste-bud micrograph metadata. Neither image was visually inspected; OpenStax taste tissue species is unstated and pathways/territories are absent.

illustrations.title: Sweat and sebaceous glands
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: the inspected sweat-gland micrograph shows glandular profiles but its organism is unconfirmed and it does not show the full human eccrine/apocrine/sebaceous arrangement; Duke's human skin slide listing was not an inspected photograph. Human counterpart remains unsupported; absence is not established.

illustrations.title: Original cell overview
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: the broad cell schematic groups membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, nucleolus and multiple organelles, but no qualifying human source-page photo with visually checked organelle coverage and provenance is present in the reviewed candidates. Unavailable evidence, not evidence that none exists.

illustrations.title: Original mitosis stages
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: the schematic spans interphase through telophase; no source-page set in the reviewed candidates visibly verifies the full sequence in human cells. A single-stage image would not cover the stages. No qualifying set verified; not a claim that none exists.

illustrations.title: Skin in section: layers, appendages and receptors
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human thin skin; real tissue section opened. Does not by itself establish every epidermal stratum, elastin fibre, sensory receptor or hypodermal structure in the composite plates. Human scalp; longitudinal follicles/bulbs and sebaceous glands visible. No claim that the overview resolves the complete papilla, sebaceous duct and arrector-pili combination. Human thick skin with a Pacinian corpuscle; no nail apparatus in the inspected field. Rejected as a nail-section match.

illustrations.title: Epidermis: strata and cell types (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human thin skin; real tissue section opened. Does not by itself establish every epidermal stratum, elastin fibre, sensory receptor or hypodermal structure in the composite plates. Human thick skin with a Pacinian corpuscle; no nail apparatus in the inspected field. Rejected as a nail-section match.

illustrations.title: Dermis and hypodermis: fibres and vessels
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human thin skin; real tissue section opened. Does not by itself establish every epidermal stratum, elastin fibre, sensory receptor or hypodermal structure in the composite plates. Human scalp; longitudinal follicles/bulbs and sebaceous glands visible. No claim that the overview resolves the complete papilla, sebaceous duct and arrector-pili combination. Human thick skin with a Pacinian corpuscle; no nail apparatus in the inspected field. Rejected as a nail-section match.

illustrations.title: Hair follicle in longitudinal section
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human scalp; longitudinal follicles/bulbs and sebaceous glands visible. No claim that the overview resolves the complete papilla, sebaceous duct and arrector-pili combination.

illustrations.title: Stratified cuboidal, columnar and transitional epithelia (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: inspected sweat-gland image is an unconfirmed-species example for a stratified gland duct only. It does not verify human stratified columnar or transitional epithelium; those panels remain unavailable.

illustrations.title: Loose connective tissues: areolar, adipose, reticular (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: the BCC page lists areolar, adipose and reticular examples but individual source photo, species, creator/terms and visual content were not verified in the audited material. All three human panels remain unsupported.

illustrations.title: Dense connective tissues: regular, irregular, elastic (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: Columbia source describes a human dense-regular tendon slide, but its photo was not visually inspected; no checked human images cover dense-irregular and elastic tissue. At most a text-level tendon lead, not a verified mapping.

illustrations.title: Cartilages: hyaline, elastic, fibrocartilage (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: the BCC mammalian-histology page is a candidate for cartilage types, but no individual photograph, human specimen identity, creator/terms or image content was verified. Hyaline, elastic and fibrocartilage human panels remain unsupported.

illustrations.title: Nervous tissue: neuron and neuroglia (schematic)
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: no reviewed candidate meets the public source-page, human provenance and image-inspection test for both neuron morphology and the represented glia. Evidence unavailable for this composite; not proof that no suitable images exist.

illustrations.title: Nail in longitudinal section
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: Duke describes a human fingertip slide, but no source photograph was visually inspected and nail plate, bed, matrix and fold structures were not confirmed. It is an index lead rather than a verified counterpart.

illustrations.title: Composition of blood: plasma, serum and formed elements
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final check: original human blood SEM was visually inspected; source caption and NCI metadata identify human circulating blood, erythrocytes, leukocytes and platelets, with Wetzel/Schaefer attribution and a public-domain note. Plasma/serum separation and clot/centrifugation panels remain unmatched.

illustrations.title: Red bone marrow and hematopoiesis
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: UNSW marrow histology photo was visually seen, but source does not establish species and its reuse terms are non-commercial; hematopoietic lineage/process schematic is not shown. No verified human counterpart.

illustrations.title: Vessel wall layers and vessel types
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: no reviewed source set provides visually inspected, human-confirmed photos for artery, vein, capillary and all depicted wall layers. This is unavailable source evidence, not proof of no public specimen images.

illustrations.title: Flow chain: aorta to vein
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: this depicts a continuous circulation route/process from aorta to vein, not a photographic specimen. No single image is a truthful literal counterpart; any future links would need to be explicitly illustrative examples, not a photo replacement.

illustrations.title: Three capillary types
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: verified human kidney cortex shows glomerular capillary profiles, a relevant example for fenestrated filtration beds. It does not cover continuous or sinusoidal types, and no ultrastructural comparison was verified.

illustrations.title: Alveolar unit: bronchiole, duct, sac and alveoli
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final check: visually inspected human alveolar-sac photo confirms alveolar air spaces/septa only. It does not show bronchiole or duct, so it remains a relevant example for the unit schematic, not a complete mapping.

illustrations.title: Respiratory membrane and airway wall
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final check: visually inspected human alveolar-sac photo shows air spaces and septa, a relevant tissue example; it does not resolve the respiratory membrane ultrastructure or airway wall, so the composite remains partial.

illustrations.title: Lymph node: afferent, sinuses, efferent and hilum
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: Duke page identifies human lymph-node histology but its linked photo was not visually inspected; node compartments plus gross afferent/efferent/sinus flow are not verified together. Evidence remains unavailable.

illustrations.title: Spleen: red pulp and white pulp
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human spleen section; red/white pulp visible. Central arteriole, marginal-zone boundary, individual sinusoids and cords were not all resolved in the overview.

illustrations.title: Thymus and thymic lobule
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human thymus; lobules, cortex and medulla visible. Hassall corpuscles and anterior chest/retrosternal placement not established by this overview.

illustrations.title: Tonsils: where they sit and how they are built
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: Duke's tonsil listing has unconfirmed organism and uninspected image; even a tissue image could not replace the gross tonsil locations. Both human tissue photo and location coverage remain unresolved.

illustrations.title: Gut-associated lymphoid tissue and the lacteal
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: the already inspected human ileal cross-section shows the prominent aggregated lymphoid tissue relevant to Peyer patches. Appendix lymphoid tissue, villus lacteals and the intestinal lymphatic-trunk route are not established together. A Peyer-patch example is not complete coverage of this composite.

illustrations.title: Endocrine glands of the body
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final check: visually inspected human pancreatic-islet micrograph supports one endocrine-tissue example; source identifies red glucagon and blue insulin staining. It does not cover the other endocrine glands, gross body map, or gonads; record remains partial.

illustrations.title: Hypothalamus and pituitary: portal and neural links
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: human pituitary slide description is relevant but photo not inspected and cannot depict portal circulation or hypothalamic nerve fibers. The process schematic has no verified photo counterpart.

illustrations.title: Thyroid and parathyroid glands
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final comparison: source text describes human thyroid/parathyroid material but no image was inspected for follicles, colloid, C cells or chief-cell clusters. Human examples remain unverified.

illustrations.title: Adrenal gland: cortex zones and medulla
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial, not approved: Human adrenal section with cortex and medulla; not an in-situ adrenal-on-kidney photograph and not cell-level verification of every cortical zone/chromaffin cell.

illustrations.title: Pancreas: exocrine acini and the endocrine islet
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Final check: the original licensed human pancreatic-islet image was visually inspected; caption identifies an islet with red glucagon and blue insulin staining, creator Afferent, CC BY-SA 3.0. It is a relevant islet example only; whole-pancreas position, acinar/duct system and delta cells are not established, so record remains partial.

illustrations.title: Gonads: ovary and testis
illustrations.unresolvedCoverageReason: Partial: the already inspected human ovarian sections include a corpus luteum and follicular profiles, so an ovarian example is established.
